Early in last summer's 200 mile big car race, Art Pollard of Medford, Ore. (#16-Thermo-King T. C. Offy)
lost his brakes going into the north turn. Hot on his exhaust stacks was Al Unser of Albuquerque, N. M. (#5-
Retzloff Chemical Ford). Pollard spun and hit the wall and Unser did likewise (see upper photo) as Wally
Dallenbach of New Brunswick, N. J., tosses a quick look as he speeds past. In the lower photo, Unser heads
for the fence as emergency crewmen of Wisconsin Auto Racing hotfoot it to the scene. Neither driver was
injured.

got ready for the race. Johncock came on to win the race, averaging more than 98 miles per hour. Pre-race
favorite Mario Andretti of Nazareth, Pa., had been knocked out of contention when his car was wrecked in a
practice session mishap started by another driver.

Harry Goode Photo
Gordon Johncock of Hastings, Mich. (#3-Gilmore Broadcasting Ford) was on the move and heading for
victory in the June 4, 150 miler here last year when this picture was taken. Gordon is a product of the rough,
tough supermodified stock car circuit in the Detroit area which also produced John Conely, Ronnie Duman,
and Gordy's cousin, Nolan Johncock. Johncock came back to finish fourth in the Aug. 20, 200 miler and won
the "outstanding driver for 1968 at Milwaukee" award given by the Miller Brewing Co.

Al Unser of Albuquerque, N. M. (#5-Retzloff Chemical Ford) had all stops pulled as he hurried through
the north turn in the June 4, 150 miler here last year. Al finished second in the 1967 Indianapolis 500 miler
and was voted "rookie of the year" in the USAC stock car division. Along with brothers Bobby, Jerry and
Louie, they comprise one of the toughest brother driving combinations in auto racing. Al was involved in
an accident later in this race with Art Pollard of Medford, Ore., but both escaped injury.

DeanVanLines Spl.
Harry Goode Photo
Mario Andretti of Nazareth, Pa. (#1-Dean Van Lines Ford) showed the form that won for him the Aug.
20, 200 miler here last summer. Andretti led from the third milé to the finish and was never in trouble at any
time. A year earlier, the talented little Italian import had won both the 100 and 200 mile big car races here.
Victory in the 200 miler last summer was worth a record $17,069 to Andretti who drove his first race at
Milwaukee in August of 1964.

Star Of Two-Wheelers Goes Great On Four
STp
Harry Goode Photo
Joe Leonard is a three-time national motorcycle racing champ. He is also one of the finest drivers on
the USAC national championship speedway car circuit. Here's Joe on his way to an eighth place finish in
the June 4, 150 miler here last summer in A. J. Foyt's car. Leonard finished second to Foyt in the 1967
Indianapolis 500 mile race, leaving the tough Texan with the pleasant job of picking up more than $214,000
in prize and accessory money.
Winning Combination For Wilke
RISLONE
RACING
Harry Goode Photo
Shades of A. J. Foyt. Here's Bobby Unser of Albuquerque, N. M., the winner of three of the first four
national championship speedway car races on the 1968 USA schedule. They were at Phoenix, Las Vegas
and Trenton. Here's Bobby last June 4 as he finished sixth in Bob Wilke's #6 Ford powered racer. Bobby's
younger brother, Al, also is a star performer on the championship trail. Bobby is 34 years old and has been
driving racing cars of all kinds since he was 15. His late brother, Jerry, was USAC stock car champ in 1957.
